TITLE: Sink: Elasticsearch `write_mode: overwrite` via alias swap
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
Add `write_mode: overwrite` support to the Elasticsearch sink. It was deliberately excluded from the initial overwrite feature (#492) because Elasticsearch has **no atomic replace of a concrete index** — a delete-then-reindex would risk data loss if the run fails mid-commit, violating the overwrite safety guarantee (a failed/cancelled run must leave the prior destination intact).

## Motivation
Overwrite (full-refresh) landed on the other 6 upsert-capable sinks (postgres, sqlite, mysql, mssql, mongodb, bigquery) in #492 with an atomic begin-stage → commit-swap lifecycle. Elasticsearch is the one holdout; completing it makes the capability uniform across all keyed-write sinks.

## Proposed design
Alias-based swap (the idiomatic ES pattern for atomic index replacement):
- `begin_overwrite`: create a fresh physical index `<index>-<runid>` (copying the target's mappings/settings), write the run into it.
- `commit_overwrite`: atomically move the read alias `<index>` from the old physical index to the new one in a single `POST _aliases` actions call (ES guarantees atomicity of alias actions), then delete the old physical index.
- `abort_overwrite`: delete the staging physical index; the alias is untouched.
- Requires the configured `index` to be (or become) an **alias**, not a concrete index — document this precondition and detect/validate it. Decide behavior when `index` is currently a concrete index (error with guidance, or one-time convert).

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/sink/elasticsearch/src/sink.rs` (implement the four lifecycle methods + `supported_write_modes` += `Overwrite`), `config.rs` if a precondition/opt-in field is needed.
- `cli/src/registry.rs` (`OVERWRITE_SINK_KINDS` += `"elasticsearch"`).
- Docs: connectors matrix, `docs/book/src/cookbook/upsert.md`, ES README; `.claude/rules/connectors.md`.
- Tests: `crates/sink/elasticsearch/tests/overwrite.rs` (container).

## Acceptance criteria
- ES overwrite atomically swaps via alias; a mid-run failure leaves the previous index/alias intact.
- The `is_subset` schema test + capability-parity test updated; `enum_variant_added` remains a non-issue (`WriteMode` is already `#[non_exhaustive]`).

TITLE: source-rest: mutual-TLS client-certificate auth
LABELS: feature,tier-2
## Summary
Let the `rest` (and `xml`/`graphql`) HTTP sources present a **client certificate + private key** (mutual TLS) on every request, including the auth token request. Configurable from inline PEM, a file path, or a `${secret:…}`/`${vault:…}` reference.

## Motivation
ADP Workforce Now (and other enterprise/gov APIs) require mTLS: the client must present a certificate the server validates. faucet's `reqwest`-based HTTP sources have no client-cert/identity config today, so ADP cannot be replicated at all — it is one of only three hard blockers in the tap-replication audit. Ties to the Primary Goal (be the fastest, most-capable way to move data between endpoints) and Third-Party Connector Friendliness.

## Proposed design
Add an optional `tls` block to the REST source config (and mirror on xml/graphql):
```yaml
source:
  type: rest
  config:
    base_url: "https://api.eu.adp.com"
    tls:
      client_cert: "${secret:adp_cert_pem}"      # PEM (cert chain), inline / file:/ secret
      client_key:  "${secret:adp_key_pem}"       # PEM private key
      # or: client_identity_pkcs12 + password
      min_version: "1.2"                          # optional
```
- Build a `reqwest::Identity` (from PEM pair or PKCS#12) once in `new()` and attach it to the shared `reqwest::Client` (`ClientBuilder::identity`). Requires the `reqwest` `native-tls`/`rustls-tls` identity feature — pick the one already enabled and gate behind a `mtls` crate feature if it pulls new deps.
- The identity must apply to **all** requests the source makes (data + any token-endpoint call). If the token is obtained via a shared `auth:` provider, the provider's HTTP client also needs the identity — decide whether mTLS lives on the source's client only (ADP applies the cert to both the token and data requests, so the provider path matters).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/config.rs` (+ `stream.rs` client build), `crates/source/xml`, `crates/source/graphql`; possibly `crates/auth` if the token request must also present the cert; `crates/core` re-exports if a shared TLS config type is introduced.

## Edge cases
Encrypted private keys (passphrase); PKCS#12 vs PEM; cert chain vs leaf; `verify_ssl:false` self-signed servers (see the separate flag); secret redaction of key material in logs/errors.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rest` source configured with a client cert/key completes a request against an mTLS-requiring endpoint (integration test via a wiremock/rustls server requiring client auth).
- Key material is never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the config/build path.
- Docs + README updated.

## Out of scope
Server-cert pinning; per-request rotating certs.

## References
Meltano tap replication audit; tap-adp (`cert=(pub,priv)` on token + data requests). Blocks: **adp**. Related sink work: #492.

Add an OAuth1 (one-legged, HMAC-SHA256) auth provider to `faucet-auth`, signing **each request** with consumer key/secret + token key/secret + realm, generating a per-request nonce/timestamp and the OAuth1 `Authorization` header.

## Motivation
NetSuite Token-Based Auth (TBA) is OAuth1 with HMAC-SHA256 — every SuiteQL/REST request carries a signature over the request method+URL+params. faucet-auth today only issues OAuth2 bearer tokens (`static`/`oauth2`/`oauth2_refresh`/`token_endpoint`), which model a *token* applied as a header, not **per-request signing**. So NetSuite cannot be replicated — one of three hard blockers in the tap audit. This is distinct from the `token_endpoint` provider: there is no token to fetch; the credential is computed fresh per request from the URL+method.

## Proposed design
The current `AuthProvider` returns a `Credential` once per token lifetime — OAuth1 needs to sign per request, so this needs a request-signing hook, not just a credential fetch. Options:
1. A new `RequestSigner` capability the HTTP sources call with `(method, url, query)` to produce the `Authorization` header — added as a defaulted trait method / optional provider capability so existing providers are unaffected.
2. Provider config:
```yaml
auth:
  netsuite:
    type: oauth1
    config:
      signature_method: HMAC-SHA256
      consumer_key: "${secret:ns_consumer_key}"
      consumer_secret: "${secret:ns_consumer_secret}"
      token: "${secret:ns_token_key}"
      token_secret: "${secret:ns_token_secret}"
      realm: "${param.account_upper}"   # NetSuite account, uppercased, - -> _
```
Reuse a maintained crate for the signature base string + HMAC (e.g. `oauth1-request` / hand-rolled HMAC-SHA256 over the RFC 5849 base string). NetSuite specifics: HMAC-**SHA256** (not the SHA1 default), realm case-sensitivity, POST body params (SuiteQL) excluded from the signature base as NetSuite expects.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/` (new `oauth1.rs` + `build_provider` arm), `crates/core/src/auth.rs` / `traits.rs` (per-request signing hook, defaulted), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (invoke the signer per request), `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (register the type).

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rest` source with an `oauth1` provider produces a valid RFC 5849 HMAC-SHA256 `Authorization` header verified by a test double; signature stable for fixed nonce/timestamp (unit-tested pure signer).
- Secrets never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the pure signing path.
- Docs + README.

## Out of scope
Three-legged OAuth1 (request/authorize/access token dance); RSA-SHA1.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-netsuite uses `requests_oauthlib.OAuth1Session` + `SIGNATURE_HMAC_SHA256`. Blocks: **netsuite** (SuiteQL). NetSuite also self-loads to BigQuery — replaced by native `write_mode` (#492), tracked separately if needed.

════════════════ #497 ════════════════
TITLE: File source: fetch + parse CSV/Excel from an authenticated HTTP/Graph URL
LABELS: feature,tier-2
## Summary
A way to **download a file (CSV/Excel) from an authenticated HTTP endpoint** (e.g. Microsoft Graph `/drive/items/{id}/content`) and parse it into records — either by extending `source-csv`/`source-parquet` to accept an authed remote URL, or a small dedicated Graph/HTTP file source.

## Motivation
OneDrive (and SharePoint "files mode") are **not** JSON record APIs — the tap authenticates to Microsoft Graph, downloads an .xlsx/.csv **blob**, and parses it (`openpyxl`/`csv.DictReader`) with header/timeseries handling. The `rest` source reads JSON responses; it cannot fetch a binary and run a CSV/Excel reader over it. So OneDrive is unreplicable — the third hard blocker in the tap audit. faucet already parses CSV/Parquet from local + S3/GCS; the missing piece is fetching the blob over an authed HTTP/Graph URL.

## Proposed design
Preferred: extend the existing file sources with a remote fetch:
```yaml
source:
  type: csv           # (or a new `http-file`)
  config:
    url: "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/{id}/items/{item}/content"
    auth: { ref: graph_onedrive }     # reuse faucet-auth (oauth2_refresh)
    format: excel                     # csv | excel
    # sheet, header_row, delimiter, glob-over-a-listing-endpoint, etc.
```
- Reuse `oauth2_refresh` for the Graph token (with rotation persistence, tracked separately).
- Excel parsing needs a reader crate (`calamine` is the standard Rust .xlsx/.xls reader) behind a feature flag.
- Support a listing step (Graph folder search) → one record-stream per matched file, or pair with `matrix` for known file ids.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/csv/` (remote fetch + optional excel via `calamine`), or a new `crates/source/http-file/`; `faucet-auth` reuse; docs + capability matrix; CI `feature-check` matrix if a new feature/crate is added.

## Edge cases
Large files (stream/range download); header detection; Excel multi-sheet + type coercion; Graph download-URL redirects (`@microsoft.graph.downloadUrl`); refresh-token rotation (see linked issue).

## Acceptance criteria
- Fetch + parse a CSV and an XLSX from an authed URL (wiremock serving fixture bytes) into the expected records.
- ≥90% patch coverage on the pure parse path; docs + README.

## Out of scope
Arbitrary binary formats beyond CSV/Excel; write-back to the file store.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-sharepointsites onedrive mode (Graph `/content` + `openpyxl`/`csv`). Blocks: **onedrive** (+ SharePoint files). Depends on refresh-token rotation persistence.

════════════════ #498 ════════════════
TITLE: faucet-auth token_endpoint: custom output header (cookie) + form-encoded body / resource param
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
Extend the existing `token_endpoint` auth provider so the fetched token can be placed in **any header** (not only `Authorization: Bearer`) and so the token request can be **form-encoded** and carry extra params (e.g. `resource=`). The provider already POSTs to an arbitrary endpoint and extracts the token via `token_path`; this is the last mile.

## Motivation
Two taps need auth flows that are *almost* covered today:
- **SAP Business One** (`tap-sap`): `POST /b1s/v1/Login {CompanyDB,UserName,Password}` returns a `SessionId` that must be carried as **`Cookie: B1SESSION=<id>; CompanyDB=<db>`** on every request — not an `Authorization` header. `token_endpoint` already fetches the id (`token_path: $.SessionId`), and `faucet_core::auth::Credential::Header { name, value }` **already** exists and the REST source already applies it as an arbitrary header. The provider just hardcodes `Credential::Bearer`.
- **Dynamics 365 F&O** (`tap-dynamics-finance`): Azure AD **v1** `/oauth2/token` with a **form-encoded** body containing `resource=https://{host}`. `oauth2` sends `scope` not `resource`; `token_endpoint` currently posts **JSON** (`req.json(body)`), which the OAuth token endpoint rejects.

Both reduce to small, additive knobs on `token_endpoint`. This is what reclassified SAP from "blocked" to "small enhancement" in the tap-replication audit.

## Proposed design
Add optional config to `token_endpoint` (`crates/auth/src/token_endpoint.rs`):
```yaml
auth:
  sap:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://host:50000/b1s/v1/Login"
      body: { CompanyDB: "${param.company_db}", UserName: "${param.user}", Password: "${param.pass}" }
      token_path: "$.SessionId"
      apply_as:                                    # NEW; default = Authorization: Bearer {token}
        header: "Cookie"
        template: "B1SESSION={token}; CompanyDB=${param.company_db}"
  fno:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${param.tenant}/oauth2/token"
      encoding: form                               # NEW; default = json
      body: { grant_type: client_credentials, client_id: "…", client_secret: "…", resource: "https://${param.subdomain}.operations.dynamics.com" }
      token_path: "$.access_token"
```
- `apply_as` → return `Credential::Header { name, value }` (already applied by `rest`) with `{token}` substituted; default keeps `Credential::Bearer`.
- `encoding: form|json` → `req.form(body)` vs `req.json(body)`.
- Optional: re-auth on a 401 (SAP sessions expire ~30 min; the tap has no re-login — faucet can be better here).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/src/token_endpoint.rs` (config + apply + encoding), `crates/core/src/auth.rs` (already has `Credential::Header`), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (already maps `Credential::Header` → `Auth::Custom`; verify multi-header/cookie value passes through), docs.


════════════════ #499 ════════════════
TITLE: faucet-auth oauth2_refresh: persist the rotated refresh_token to the state store
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
When an OAuth2 provider (e.g. Microsoft, Rippling) **rotates the refresh_token** on each refresh, `oauth2_refresh` must persist the new refresh_token durably so the *next* run authenticates. Today rotation is handled in-memory only, so a second scheduled run 401s.

## Motivation
- **Rippling** (`tap-rippling`): rotates the refresh_token on every refresh; the tap writes the new one to `/tmp/refresh_token.txt` for the next ECS run. A faucet `oauth2_refresh` provider that rotates in-memory works for one run but the next run presents the now-invalidated original → 401.
- **OneDrive** (`tap-sharepointsites` onedrive mode): same — Microsoft rotates the refresh_token each use.

This is a reliability gap: single-run replicas pass, scheduled/repeated runs fail. Ties to the Primary Goal (reliability).

## Proposed design
- Give `oauth2_refresh` an optional durable store hook so it can write the rotated `refresh_token` (and expiry) back. Reuse the pipeline's `StateStore` (the same durable backend used for bookmarks) under a dedicated key, e.g. `auth:oauth2_refresh:<provider-name>`.
- On startup, read the stored refresh_token (if present) in preference to the config's seed value; on each rotation, atomically persist the new one.
- Must be safe across concurrent rows sharing one provider (single-flight already exists) and across process restarts.
- Config: opt-in `persist: true` (or automatic when a state store is configured), referencing the run's state backend.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/src/oauth2.rs` (`OAuth2RefreshProvider`), a bridge to `faucet_core::StateStore`, `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (wire the state backend into provider construction), docs.

## Edge cases
Provider shared by N matrix rows (persist once, single-flight); first run with only a seed token; store unavailable (fail closed vs warn); secret redaction of the persisted token.

## Acceptance criteria
- A simulated rotating token endpoint: run 1 rotates + persists; run 2 (fresh process/provider) reads the persisted token and authenticates (integration test with a wiremock rotating endpoint + a file/memory state store).
- Token never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the persistence path.

## Out of scope
Non-rotating providers (unaffected); OAuth1.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-rippling `REFRESH_TOKEN_FILE`, tap-sharepointsites onedrive rotation. Unblocks: **rippling, onedrive**.

════════════════ #500 ════════════════
TITLE: source-rest: POST-search pagination (cursor + filter in the request body)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
Add a REST pagination style for **POST search** endpoints where the next-page cursor (and the incremental filter) live **in the request JSON body**, not in a query param or a next-link. The paginator must inject the extracted cursor back into the body for the next request.

## Motivation
- **HubSpot CRM** (`tap-hubspot`): reads objects via `POST /crm/v3/objects/{obj}/search` with a JSON body `{filterGroups, limit, sorts, properties, after}`; the next cursor is `$.paging.next.after` and is placed back into `payload.after`. The incremental filter (`hs_lastmodifieddate GTE …`) is also in the body. faucet's `rest` source supports POST + body, but its pagination styles (Cursor/PageNumber/Offset/LinkHeader/NextLinkInBody) all advance a **query param or next-link**, not a body field.
- **NetSuite SuiteQL** (`tap-netsuite`) posts `{"q":"SELECT …"}` with offset/limit — a related body-driven pattern (though offset there is a URL param).

Without this, HubSpot's core object streams can't paginate faithfully.

## Proposed design
A new `PaginationStyle::CursorInBody` (name TBD) on the REST source:
```yaml
pagination:
  type: CursorInBody
  next_token_path: "$.paging.next.after"     # where the next cursor is read from the response
  body_cursor_field: "after"                 # where to write it into the next request body
  # stops when next_token_path is null/absent; loop-guard on repeated token (as Cursor does)
```
- Reuse the existing cursor loop-detection + `max_pages` cap.
- The initial body comes from `source.config.body`; each subsequent request sets `body[body_cursor_field] = <extracted cursor>`.
- Consider a companion for HubSpot's 10k-result `hs_object_id GT <last>` re-filter (a secondary body mutation when a page count threshold is hit) — could be a follow-up.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/pagination/` (new module + `PaginationStyle` variant + `advance` handling that mutates the body), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (thread the body mutation into the next request), docs (pagination table in `.claude/rules/connectors.md` + the docs site).

## Acceptance criteria
- A wiremock POST-search endpoint returning `paging.next.after` paginates to completion, injecting the cursor into the body each page; loop guard + `max_pages` honored. Unit + integration tests.
- ≥90% patch coverage.

## Out of scope
GraphQL (has its own source); the HubSpot 10k re-filter (separate follow-up); dynamic property discovery (separate).

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-hubspot object search. Unblocks: **hubspot** (core objects); related: **netsuite** SuiteQL. Pagination styles: `.claude/rules/connectors.md`.

════════════════ #501 ════════════════
TITLE: CLI: discovery-driven request matrix (fan out over dimensions fetched at plan time)
LABELS: feature,tier-3
## Summary
Let a matrix fan out over a **dimension set discovered at plan time from another endpoint/query**, not just a static list. i.e. "run this stream once per {company / subsidiary / custom-field / list-id} returned by a discovery call."

## Motivation
Several taps compute their request set from a *live* enumeration before syncing:
- **Rillet report streams** (`tap-rillet`): month windows **×** subsidiary ids **×** custom-field ids, where the id lists are fetched from `/subsidiaries`, `/fields`, and a `/reports/balance-sheet?breakdown_by=SUBSIDIARY` probe at plan time.
- **Dynamics 365 BC** (`tap-dynamics-business-central`): `GET /companies` then every entity is fanned out per company × environment.
- **BambooHR** custom reports, **HubSpot** child associations — similar "enumerate then fan out" shapes.

faucet's `matrix` supports static rows and parent→child fan-out over *records the parent stream emitted*, but not "fan out over the distinct values of a discovery query/endpoint" as a first-class, cached, plan-time step. This is the single biggest structural gap for report-style taps.

## Proposed design (sketch — needs design discussion)
A matrix row (or a new pre-step) that declares a discovery source and a projection:
```yaml
matrix:
  - id: subsidiaries          # discovery step
    discover:
      source: { type: rest, config: { path: "/subsidiaries", records_path: "$.subsidiaries[*]" } }
      as: subsidiary_id
      select: "$.id"
  - id: trial_balance
    for_each: subsidiaries    # one invocation per discovered subsidiary_id
    source: { config: { path: "/reports/trial-balance", query_params: { subsidiary_id: "${subsidiaries.subsidiary_id}" } } }
```
- Discovery runs once, results cached; the dependent rows expand to N invocations (compose with the existing `${now.*}` / backfill month windows for the cross-product).
- Overlaps with `faucet discover` (#211) and the parent/child matrix — evaluate whether this is a new matrix mode or an extension of `parent:`.

## Affected crates / files
`cli/src/expand.rs` / `executor.rs` (plan-time discovery + fan-out), `cli/src/config.rs` (grammar), docs. Likely reuses `Source::discover` where a catalog exists, else a generic "distinct values of a query" step.

## Acceptance criteria
- A config that fans a stream out over the ids returned by a discovery call produces N invocations, cached once; composes with `matrix` date windows. Tests on the pure planning logic.

## Out of scope (v1)
The deep report-tree flattening that follows (that's a transform, tracked separately); recursion.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-rillet report fan-out, tap-dynamics-business-central company enumeration. Related: #211 (discover), matrix parent/child. Partial for: **rillet reports, ms365bc**.

════════════════ #502 ════════════════
TITLE: source: completeness reconciliation (rows fetched vs authoritative count)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
An opt-in guard that compares the number of rows a source actually fetched against an **authoritative count** for the same filter, and fails the run on a shortfall beyond a tolerance — catching silent truncation (a half-read table quietly overwriting a full one).

## Motivation
- **Dynamics 365 F&O** (`tap-dynamics-finance`): after each stream it issues OData `$count=true&$top=0`, reads `@odata.count`, and compares against the distinct-PK count fetched; a shortfall beyond `source_count_recon_tolerance_pct` raises `SilentTruncationError` and fails the tap. This exists specifically because offset/skip paging can silently truncate a full-refresh — exactly the scenario `write_mode: overwrite` (#492) makes dangerous (a truncated read would replace good data with less).

faucet has SLA `min_rows_per_run` (#202) and volume anomaly detection, which partially cover the intent, but not a per-run *authoritative count* comparison for a specific source.

## Proposed design
- A source-level (or pipeline-level) `reconcile:` option: after the run, fetch a count via a configured probe (OData `$count`, a SQL `SELECT count(*)`, etc.) over the same filter, compare to rows emitted, and fail if `fetched < count * (1 - tolerance)`.
- Compose with `write_mode: overwrite` so an overwrite never truncates on a short read.
- For sources without a native count, this is a no-op / not offered.

## Affected crates / files
Likely a CLI-layer post-run check (like SLA in `cli/src/sla/`) that can issue a count probe, or a `Source` capability method `estimated/exact count`. Reuse `faucet_core::discover::estimated_rows` where present. Docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- A source that under-reads (simulated) fails the run when reconcile is on and the shortfall exceeds tolerance; passes within tolerance. Pure comparison logic unit-tested.

## Out of scope
Per-partition recon internals (F&O also reconciles each key-range — a follow-up); sources with no count.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-dynamics-finance `$count` recon + `SilentTruncationError`. Related: SLA #202, overwrite #492. Strengthens: all overwrite/full-refresh runs; directly: **ms365fno**.

════════════════ #503 ════════════════
TITLE: source-rest: stop pagination on HTTP 204 No Content
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
Add `204 No Content` as a pagination stop condition for the REST source's offset/skip paginator.

## Motivation
- **ADP** (`tap-adp`): paginates with OData `$top`/`$skip` and stops when the server returns **`204 No Content`** (rather than an empty JSON array). faucet's offset paginator stops on a zero-record page / offset≥total, not on a 204 status.

Minor, but it's the difference between a faithful ADP replica and an extra empty request or a hang.

## Proposed design
- In the REST source's pagination loop, treat a `204` response (empty body) as a terminal "no more pages" signal for the offset/page styles (and arguably all styles). Guard so a 204 mid-stream ends cleanly rather than erroring on empty-body JSON parse.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (response handling) + `pagination/` stop conditions; docs (pagination table).

## Acceptance criteria
- A wiremock endpoint returning rows then a `204` terminates pagination without error and without an extra empty page. Unit/integration test.

## Out of scope
Non-204 empty-signal conventions.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-adp `ADPPaginator` stops on 204. Part of the ADP replica (mTLS is the hard blocker, see the mTLS issue).

## Custom token endpoint

For non-standard token endpoints, `token_endpoint` lets you describe the request
and point at the access-token and expiry fields in the response. See
`faucet schema source rest` for the full field list.

Two knobs cover the less-standard flows:

- **`encoding: form`** sends the token request as
  `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (OAuth endpoints that expect a `resource=`
  param need this; the default is `json`).
- **`apply_as: { header, template }`** puts the fetched token in an arbitrary
  header instead of `Authorization: Bearer` — e.g. a session cookie. `template`
  is the header value with `{token}` substituted.

```yaml
auth:
  sap:                          # SAP B1: SessionId carried as a cookie
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://host:50000/b1s/v1/Login"
      body: { CompanyDB: "${param.company_db}", UserName: "${param.user}", Password: "${secret:sap_pw}" }
      token_path: "$.SessionId"
      apply_as: { header: "Cookie", template: "B1SESSION={token}; CompanyDB=${param.company_db}" }
```

## Persisting a rotating refresh token

Some providers (Microsoft Graph, Rippling) **rotate the `refresh_token` on every
refresh** — the old one is invalidated. In-memory rotation works for a single
run, but the *next* scheduled run would present the now-stale seed and get a 401.
Set `persist.path` on an `oauth2_refresh` provider to durably store the rotated
token (a file-backed state store) so later runs pick up where the last one left
off:

```yaml
auth:
  graph:
    type: oauth2_refresh
    config:
      token_url: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${param.tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token"
      client_id: "${secret:graph_client_id}"
      client_secret: "${secret:graph_client_secret}"
      refresh_token: "${secret:graph_seed_refresh_token}"   # seed; used only until the first rotation
      persist:
        path: "./state/auth"      # rotated refresh_token survives across runs
```
